_about: Locked gate thresholds (CORE-1169 part 1). The lexical gate is deterministic and independent of any model/judge. Tuned on the baseline run; do not loosen without recording why.

judge._note: secondary / flag-only: never auto-fails the headline unless the lexical gate also fails

jargon._note: the BINARY jargon gate uses the sharp rarity/AoA cutoff (precision-critical); Dale-Chall is a graded signal in the difficulty score, not a binary trigger, to avoid over-flagging ordinary off-list words. jargon.py reads these values (single source of truth).
jargon._audit_core_1169_part1b: hard_zipf lowered 3.0 -> 2.6 after a live run over-flagged mid-frequency words a fluent adult knows (murmur 2.92, predictability 2.85, passivity 2.60, argumentation 2.65, ephemeral 2.99). At 2.6 the canonical academic-register failures still flag (solemnity 2.54, litotes 1.23, deontological 1.88, apperception 1.77, professionalization 2.03, iconographic 2.16). The ~2.3-2.9 band is register-dependent (rarity alone cannot separate 'solemnity' jargon from 'passivity' plain) -- the human calibration step (calibrate.py + the worksheet) measures kappa there before this referees any prompt.
jargon._aoa_note: hard_aoa is inactive while vendor/aoa_kuperman.csv is absent (aoa() returns None); it stays documented for when the Kuperman norms are present.
